newsitem.title: UK: Gold rebounds, oil firm in volatile commodities.
newsitem.headline: Gold rebounds, oil firm in volatile commodities.

text.p: Weaker U.S. share values and an easier dollar helped the price of gold to rebound after its fall to the lowest in three years earlier this week.
Oil prices edged higher on tight prompt supply. Wheat was little changed and copper less volatile.

Gold had fallen to its lowest in three years on Tuesday, down at $365.95 an ounce. Speculators abandoned it and mining companies sold heavily, while brokers also reported talk that a central bank might have been selling too.

But Tuesday's drop of 79 points on the Dow Jones industrial average triggered a short covering rally led by investment funds and gold was fixed more than $3.00 firmer in London on Wednesday afternoon at $370.90.
Dealers, however, said gold remained vulnerable and it eased later to around $369. Crude oil was firm, trading in London's Wednesday afternoon just above $23.85 per barrel.
Tight supply and strong U.S. heating fuel demand kept a floor under the firm price despite news of a build in U.S. stocks of refined product.
Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) wheat futures were little changed toward mid-session just below $3.84 per bushel.
London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices consolidated after recent volatility with the benchmark three-months delivery trading just above $2,200 per tonne in late activity.
Aluminium moved slightly higher to find commission house selling. Metals await the next LME stocks data due on Friday.

Cocoa futures met profit taking and sales from origin countries to cap a brisk advance seen on Tuesday. The London benchmark March futures contract reached 950 pounds sterling per tonne then eased to close at 933 pounds.
Coffee extended a decline.

Far East origin sellers moved to lock in current prices on a perception that the decline would continue, depressing the London robusta March futures price to $1,272 per tonne from $1,339 on Tuesday. Selling again hit sugar futures. The London white sugar contract eased to $297.50 after breaking support at $300 per tonne on Tuesday.
